DGP Dossier: synth_heavytail

1. Identity & Status

DGP ID synth_heavytail
Version 1.6.0
Status stable
Difficulty ★★★☆☆ (3/5)
Stress Profile  overlap: moderatenoise: heavylinearity: lineareffect: lineartarget: both

2. What This DGP Stresses (Intent)

Purpose: Penalize estimators that rely on L2 loss under heavy-tailed noise.

This DGP is identical to the baseline linear design except for the outcome noise, which is a Gaussian/Cauchy mixture. The Cauchy component makes the population mean of observed outcomes undefined, so any estimator that minimizes squared error is theoretically ill-posed and will suffer variance explosion.

This motivates robust estimators (e.g., median/quantile targets) that remain well-defined under heavy tails.

3. Identification Assumptions (Explicit)

  • Unconfoundedness holds by construction (treatment is assigned by a known propensity score).
  • Overlap is moderate (p(X) bounded away from 0 and 1 for most of the mass).
  • Structural ATT is defined as the mean of the signal tau(X) on treated units (Constitution Article I), independent of realized noise.

4. Mathematical Specification

Covariates \[ X \sim \mathcal{N}(0, I_5) \]

Propensity \[ p(X) = \text{expit}(0.5 X_1 - 0.5 X_2) \]

Baseline Outcome and Treatment Effect \[ \mu_0(X) = 1 + X_1 + 0.5 X_2 \] \[ \tau(X) = 1 + 0.5 X_1 \]

Noise Mixture (Heavy Tails) \[ \varepsilon \sim 0.8 \cdot \mathcal{N}(0, 0.5^2) + 0.2 \cdot \text{Cauchy}(0, 1) \] where \(\varepsilon_0\) and \(\varepsilon_1\) are drawn independently.

Moment note: The Cauchy component has undefined mean and variance. Therefore the population mean of realized outcomes is undefined, and any L2/MSE estimator is not well-posed in the population.

Potential Outcomes \[ Y_0 = \mu_0(X) + \varepsilon_0,\quad Y_1 = \mu_0(X) + \tau(X) + \varepsilon_1 \]

5. Oracle Truth Definition

  • ATT (Structural): \(\mathbb{E}[\tau(X) \mid W=1]\), computed from the deterministic signal \(\tau(X)\). This is well-defined even when \(\mathbb{E}[Y]\) is not.
  • QST (Distributional): computed on the canonical tau grid via oracle Monte Carlo as specified in cs_get_oracle_qst().

6. Visual Diagnostics (n = 5000)

7. Empirical Validation

We run light validation with n = 1000 and seeds = 1:20. The goal is to show variance explosion for OLS under L2 loss. We do not run heavier robust estimators here to keep doc builds fast.

Empirical validation (n=1000, seeds=1:20)
estimator_id mean_bias rmse
lm_att 3.801 9.684
oracle_att 0.000 0.000

Interpretation: OLS fails not because it is biased in the limit, but because its variance is infinite under a Cauchy mixture. The RMSE will fluctuate wildly across seeds (typical values ~8.0 in quick runs). The oracle estimator remains stable, confirming the truth layer.

8. Failure Mode Summary

  • L2-based estimators (OLS/IPW with mean targets): variance explosion; unstable RMSE.
  • Robust estimators (median/quantile targets): well-defined under heavy tails.

Appendix: Implementation

Source code for: dgp_synth_heavytail_v160

function(n, seed = NULL, include_truth = TRUE, oracle_only = FALSE) {
  if (!is.null(seed)) {
    cs_set_rng(seed)
  }

  X1 <- stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
  X2 <- stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
  if (!isTRUE(oracle_only)) {
    X3 <- stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
    X4 <- stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
    X5 <- stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 1)
  }

  mu0 <- 1 + X1 + 0.5 * X2
  tau <- 1 + 0.5 * X1
  p <- stats::plogis(0.5 * X1 - 0.5 * X2)

  w <- stats::rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = p)

  mix_ind0 <- stats::rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.8)
  eps0 <- ifelse(
    mix_ind0 == 1L,
    stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 0.5),
    stats::rcauchy(n, location = 0, scale = 1)
  )

  if (isTRUE(oracle_only)) {
    # CRN: Lock error term to eliminate MC variance and regime mismatch
    eps1 <- eps0
  } else {
    mix_ind1 <- stats::rbinom(n, size = 1, prob = 0.8)
    eps1 <- ifelse(
      mix_ind1 == 1L,
      stats::rnorm(n, mean = 0, sd = 0.5),
      stats::rcauchy(n, location = 0, scale = 1)
    )
  }

  y0 <- mu0 + eps0
  y1 <- mu0 + tau + eps1

  if (isTRUE(oracle_only)) {
    return(list(df = tibble::tibble(w = w, y0 = y0, y1 = y1)))
  }
  y <- ifelse(w == 1L, y1, y0)

  true_att <- cs_true_att(structural_te = tau, w = w)
  true_qst <- if (isTRUE(include_truth)) cs_get_oracle_qst("synth_heavytail", version = "1.6.0") else NULL

  out <- list(
    df = tibble::tibble(
      y  = y,
      w  = w,
      y0 = y0,
      y1 = y1,
      p  = p,
      structural_te = tau,
      X1 = X1,
      X2 = X2,
      X3 = X3,
      X4 = X4,
      X5 = X5
    ),
    true_att = true_att,
    true_qst = true_qst,
    meta = list(
      dgp_id        = "synth_heavytail",
      version       = "1.6.0",
      type          = "synthetic",
      params        = list(n = n, seed = seed),
      structural_te = tau
    )
  )

  cs_check_dgp_synthetic(out)

  out
}
